<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est jam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est jam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est jam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est jam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est jam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est jam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Lucam
<r>Luc 1:26-38</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Missus est Angelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilǽæ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam viro, cui nomen erat Joseph, de domo David, et nomen Vírginis María. Et réliqua.

Homilía sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi
<r>Liber 2 in Lucam</r>
<c>L</c>atent quidem divína mystéria, nec fácile, juxta prophéticum dictum, quisquam hóminum potest scire consílium Dei. Sed tamen ex céteris factis, atque præcéptis Dómini Salvatóris póssumus intellégere, et hoc propensióris fuísse consílii, quod ea potíssimum elécta est, ut Dóminum páreret, quæ erat desponsáta viro. Cur autem non ántequam desponsarétur, impléta est? Fortásse ne dicerétur quod concéperat ex adultério.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Clama in fortitúdine, qui annúntias pacem in Jerúsalem:
* Dic civitátibus Judæ, et habitatóribus Sion: Ecce Deus noster, quem exspectabámus, advéniet.
<r>℣.</r> Supra montem excélsum ascénde tu, qui evangelízas Sion, exálta in fortitúdine vocem tuam.
<r>℟.</r> Dic civitátibus Judæ, et habitatóribus Sion: Ecce Deus noster, quem exspectabámus, advéniet.

<h>Reading 1</h>
From the Holy Gospel according to Luke
<r>Luke 1:26-38</r>
<c>A</c>t that time the angel Gabriel was sent from God into a city of Galilee, called Nazareth, To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary. And so on.

Homily by St. Ambrose, Bishop <n>of Milan.</n>
<r>Bk. ii on Luke</r>
<c>T</c>he mysteries of God are unsearchable, and it is especially declared by a Prophet, that a man can hardly know His counsels. <n>Wisd. ix. 13.</n> Nevertheless, some things have been revealed to us, and we may gather from some of the words and works of the Lord our Saviour, that there was a special purpose of God, in the fact that she who was chosen to be the mother of the Lord was espoused to a man. Why did not the power of the Highest overshadow her before she was so espoused? Perhaps it was lest any might blasphemously say that she had conceived in fornication the Holy One.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> O thou that bringest good tidings of peace to Jerusalem, lift up thy voice with strength!
* Say unto the cities of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Behold, our God will come, for Whom we waited.
<r>℣.</r> O thou that tellest good tidings to Zion, get thee up into the high mountain, lift up thy voice with strength.
<r>℟.</r> Say unto the cities of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Behold, our God will come, for Whom we waited.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<c>E</c>t ingréssus ad eam Angelus. Disce vírginem móribus, disce vírginem verecúndia, disce oráculo, disce mystério. Trepidáre vírginum est, et ad omnes viri ingréssus pavére, omnes viri affátus veréri. Discant mulíeres propósitum pudóris imitári. Sola in penetrálibus, quam nemo virórum víderit, solus Angelus repérerit: sola sine cómite, sola sine teste, ne quo degénere depravarétur affátu, ab Angelo salutátur.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<c>A</c>nd the angel came in unto her. Let us learn from this Virgin how to bear ourselves, let us learn her modesty, let us learn by her devout utterance, above all let us learn by the holy mystery enacted. It is the part of a maiden to be timid, to avoid the advances of men, and to shrink from men's addresses. Would that our women would learn from the example of modesty here set before us. She upon whom the stare of men had never been fixed was alone in her chamber, and was found only by an angel. There was neither companion nor witness there, that what passed might not be debased in gossip and the angel saluted her.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> There shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Man shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite through all the princes of the aliens.
* And all the earth shall be His possession.
<r>℣.</r> Et all kings shall fall down before Him, all nations shall serve Him.
<r>℟.</r> And all the earth shall be His possession.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>T</c>anti namque mandáti mystérium non hóminis fuit, sed Angeli ore proméndum. Hódie primum audítur: Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te. Et audítur, et créditur. Dénique, Ecce, inquit, ancílla Dómini: contíngat mihi secúndum verbum tuum. Vide humilitátem, vide devotiónem. Ancíllam se dicit Dómini, quæ mater elígitur: nec repentíno exaltáta promísso est.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

b.773f54a594:
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
<r>Benediction.</r> May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<c>T</c>he message of God to the Virgin was a mystery, which it was not lawful for the mouth of men, but only of angels, to utter. For the first time on earth the words are spoken The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee. The holy maiden heareth, and believeth. At length she saith Behold the handmaid of the Lord be it unto me according to thy word. Here is an example of lowliness, here is a pattern of true devotion. At the very moment that she is told she is chosen to be the mother of the Lord she at once declareth herself His handmaid. The knowledge that she was Mother of God caused in the heart of Mary only an act of humility.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The Lord shall go forth and fight against the nations.
* And His feet shall stand upon the mount of Olives on the east.
<r>℣.</r> And it shall be exalted above the hills, and all nations shall flow unto it.
<r>℟.</r> And His feet shall stand upon the mount of Olives on the east.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> And His feet shall stand upon the mount of Olives on the east.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>D</c>écimo séptimo Kaléndas Ianuárii Luna duodevicésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>ancti Eusébii, Epíscopi Vercellénsis et Mártyris; cujus dies natális Kaléndis Augústi, et Ordinátio décimo octávo Kaléndas Ianuárii refértur.
<h>S</h>anctórum Trium Puerórum, id est Ananíæ, Azaríæ et Misaélis; quorum córpora apud Babylóniam, sub quodam specu, sunt pósita.
<h>R</h>avénnæ sanctórum Mártyrum Valentíni, magístri mílitum, ejúsque fílii Concórdii, atque Navális et Agrícolæ; qui, in persecutióne Maximiáni, pro Christo passi sunt.
<h>F</h>órmiis, in Campánia, sanctæ Albínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, sub Décio Imperatóre.
<h>I</h>n Africa pássio plurimárum sanctárum Vírginum, quæ, in persecutióne Wandálica, sub Ariáno Rege Hunneríco, suspéndia, póndera laminásque ignítas perpéssæ, martýrii agónem felíciter consummárunt.
<h>V</h>iénnæ, in Gállia, beáti Adónis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>I</h>n Hibérnia sancti Beáni Epíscopi.
<h>G</h>azæ, in Palæstína, sancti Ireniónis Epíscopi.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.567ee30e15:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 16th 2027, the 18th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy martyr Eusebius, Bishop of Vercelli, of whom mention is made upon the 1st day of August, (when he died between the years 370 and 375,) and whose ordination is recorded upon the 15th day of this present month of December.
<h>U</h>pon the same 16th day of December, were born into the better life:
<h>T</h>he three children Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, whose bodies are laid in a certain cave at Babylon (in the sixth century before Christ.)
<h>A</h>t Ravenna, the holy martyrs Valentine, a military instructor, Concordius his son, Navalis, and Agricola, who suffered for Christ's sake, (in the fourth century,) in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian.
<h>A</h>t Nola, in Campania, in the persecution under the Emperor Decius, the holy Virgin and martyr Albina, (in the year 250.)
<h>I</h>n Africa, many holy Virgins and martyrs, who in the Vandal persecution under the Arian king Hunneric suffered hanging, pressing, and redhot plates, and happily brought to a close the conflict of martyrdom, (in the year 482.)
<h>A</h>t Vienne, (in the year 875,) the blessed Confessor Ado, (monk of the Order of St Benedict,) Bishop (of Vienne.)
<h>A</h>t Aberdeen, in Scotland, holy Bean, (called first) Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Gaza, in Palestine, (in the year 389,) holy Bishop Irenion.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
